abstract.para: Currently, &docker; does not provide a built-in mechanism to launch a container directly into a highly isolated CPU set (cpuset). To achieve true deterministic performance for real-time workloads , you must perform this isolation manually.

topic.para: The process involves two primary phases:

listitem.para: Establishing the shield: Creating an isolated cgroup partition and moving all host system processes (vusing &systemd;) away from your dedicated real-time CPUs.
Migrating the container: Launching the &docker; container, and then manually migrating its processes into the newly isolated cgroup.

section.title: Establishing the shield
section.para: The following shell script brings an isolated shield up or down. It restricts default system services to CPUs 0-3, routes interrupts away from the real-time cores, and creates an isolated partition (/sys/fs/cgroup/rtcpus) for CPUs 4-63.
section.screen:
#!/bin/sh # ------------------------------------------------------------------ # Toggle script for establishing a cgroups v2 real-time shield # ------------------------------------------------------------------
let START_CPU=4 let END_CPU=63 let ONLINE=1 let SHIELD_UP=0 GOVERNOR="performance"
# Masks for routing interrupts DEFAULT_MASK=ffffffff,ffffffff SHIELD_MASK=00000000,0000000f # CPUs 0-3
CGROUP2_ROOT="/sys/fs/cgroup" SHIELD_CG="${CGROUP2_ROOT}/rtcpus"
# Capture kernel settings if [ -f /proc/sys/kernel/sched_rt_runtime_us ]; then RT_RUNTIME=$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/sched_rt_runtime_us) fi if [ -f /proc/sys/kernel/nmi_watchdog ]; then NMI_WATCHDOG=$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/nmi_watchdog) fi
# Detect if the shield is already active if [ -d "$SHIELD_CG" ]; then let SHIELD_UP=1 fi
if [ $SHIELD_UP -eq 1 ]; then echo "Tearing down cgroup v2 shield..."
# 1. Dismantle the isolated partition if [ -f "${SHIELD_CG}/cpuset.cpus.partition" ]; then echo "member" > "${SHIELD_CG}/cpuset.cpus.partition" 2>/dev/null fi
# 2. Move any leftover tasks back to the root cgroup if [ -f "${SHIELD_CG}/cgroup.procs" ]; then for pid in $(cat "${SHIELD_CG}/cgroup.procs" 2>/dev/null); do echo $pid > "${CGROUP2_ROOT}/cgroup.procs" 2>/dev/null done fi
# 3. Remove the custom cgroup rmdir "$SHIELD_CG" 2>/dev/null
# 4. Restore systemd slices to use all CPUs systemctl set-property --runtime system.slice AllowedCPUs=0-63 systemctl set-property --runtime user.slice AllowedCPUs=0-63 systemctl set-property --runtime init.scope AllowedCPUs=0-63
# Restore default IRQ affinity echo ${DEFAULT_MASK} > /proc/irq/default_smp_affinity for irqlist in $(ls /proc/irq/*/smp_affinity 2>/dev/null); do echo ${DEFAULT_MASK} >$irqlist 2>/dev/null done
# Restore kernel tuning (Timers, Hugepages, Watchdogs, etc.) [ -f /proc/sys/kernel/timer_migration ] && echo 1 > /proc/sys/kernel/timer_migration [ -f /proc/sys/kernel/sched_rt_runtime_us ] && echo ${RT_RUNTIME} > /proc/sys/kernel/sched_rt_runtime_us [ -f /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/tracing_on ] && echo 1 > /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/tracing_on [ -f /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled ] && echo always > /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled [ -f /proc/sys/kernel/nmi_watchdog ] && echo ${NMI_WATCHDOG} > /proc/sys/kernel/nmi_watchdog [ -f /sys/devices/system/machinecheck/machinecheck0/check_interval ] && echo 300 > /sys/devices/system/machinecheck/machinecheck0/check_interval [ -f /sys/devices/virtual/workqueue/writeback/cpumask ] && echo ${DEFAULT_MASK} > /sys/devices/virtual/workqueue/writeback/cpumask [ -f /sys/devices/virtual/workqueue/cpumask ] && echo ${DEFAULT_MASK} > /sys/devices/virtual/workqueue/cpumask [ -f /proc/sys/vm/stat_interval ] && echo 1 > /proc/sys/vm/stat_interval [ -f /sys/module/processor/parameters/latency_factor ] && echo 2 > /sys/module/processor/parameters/latency_factor [ -f /sys/module/processor/parameters/ignore_ppc ] && echo 0 > /sys/module/processor/parameters/ignore_ppc [ -f /sys/module/processor/parameters/ignore_tpc ] && echo 0 > /sys/module/processor/parameters/ignore_tpc
if [ -f /etc/init.d/sgi_irqbalance ]; then /etc/init.d/sgi_irqbalance start elif systemctl is-active --quiet irqbalance; then systemctl start irqbalance fi
else echo "Bringing up cgroup v2 shield..."
# Route IRQs away from shielded CPUs if [ -f /etc/init.d/sgi_irqbalance ]; then /etc/init.d/sgi_irqbalance stop else systemctl stop irqbalance 2>/dev/null fi
echo $SHIELD_MASK > /proc/irq/default_smp_affinity for irqlist in $(ls /proc/irq/*/smp_affinity 2>/dev/null); do echo $SHIELD_MASK >$irqlist 2>/dev/null done
# Apply Real-Time kernel tuning (Disable tracing, THP, watchdogs, etc.) [ -f /proc/sys/kernel/sched_rt_runtime_us ] && echo -1 > /proc/sys/kernel/sched_rt_runtime_us [ -f /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/tracing_on ] && echo 0 > /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/tracing_on [ -f /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled ] && echo never > /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled [ -f /proc/sys/kernel/nmi_watchdog ] && echo 0 > /proc/sys/kernel/nmi_watchdog [ -f /sys/devices/system/machinecheck/machinecheck0/check_interval ] && echo 0 > /sys/devices/system/machinecheck/machinecheck0/check_interval [ -f /sys/devices/virtual/workqueue/writeback/cpumask ] && echo ${SHIELD_MASK} > /sys/devices/virtual/workqueue/writeback/cpumask [ -f /sys/devices/virtual/workqueue/cpumask ] && echo ${SHIELD_MASK} > /sys/devices/virtual/workqueue/cpumask [ -f /proc/sys/vm/stat_interval ] && echo 999999 > /proc/sys/vm/stat_interval [ -f /sys/module/processor/parameters/latency_factor ] && echo 1 > /sys/module/processor/parameters/latency_factor [ -f /sys/module/processor/parameters/ignore_ppc ] && echo 1 > /sys/module/processor/parameters/ignore_ppc [ -f /sys/module/processor/parameters/ignore_tpc ] && echo 1 > /sys/module/processor/parameters/ignore_tpc
# 1. Restrict default system tasks to non-shielded CPUs using systemd systemctl set-property --runtime system.slice AllowedCPUs=0-3 systemctl set-property --runtime user.slice AllowedCPUs=0-3 systemctl set-property --runtime init.scope AllowedCPUs=0-3
# 2. Fire up the shield using native cgroups v2 mkdir -p "$SHIELD_CG"
# Ensure the cpuset controller is enabled in the subtree echo "+cpuset" > "${CGROUP2_ROOT}/cgroup.subtree_control" 2>/dev/null || true
# Assign the real-time CPUs to our shield echo "${START_CPU}-${END_CPU}" > "${SHIELD_CG}/cpuset.cpus"
# Set the partition to 'isolated' (disables load balancing across these CPUs) if [ -f "${SHIELD_CG}/cpuset.cpus.partition" ]; then echo "isolated" > "${SHIELD_CG}/cpuset.cpus.partition" fi
# Allow time for the kernel sched_domain to rebuild sleep 1
# Offline/online cycle to migrate timers and kthreads off shielded cores if [ $ONLINE -eq 1 ]; then for i in `seq ${START_CPU} ${END_CPU}`; do echo 0 > /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu$i/online echo 1 > /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu$i/online done
# Prioritize re-initialized kthreads systemctl restart set_kthread_prio 2>/dev/null || true fi
if [ -f /proc/sys/kernel/timer_migration ]; then echo 0 > /proc/sys/kernel/timer_migration fi
GOVERNOR="performance" fi
# Set CPUFreq scaling governor if [ -f /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_governor ]; then CURRENT_GOVERNOR=$(cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_governor) if ! [ "$GOVERNOR" = "$CURRENT_GOVERNOR" ]; then for i in $(ls /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor 2>/dev/null); do echo $GOVERNOR >$i done fi fi

section.title: Migrating the container into the shield
section.para: Once your rtcpus isolated cgroup is actively running, you can launch your Docker workload. The workflow below demonstrates how to initialize the container and seamlessly transfer its PID into the shielded partition.
The script below uses the script created in the previous section called shield.sh. If you named it differently, please add just the code below accordingly.
section.screen:
# 1. Execute the shield script to isolate CPUs 4-63 ./shield.sh
# 2. Launch your real-time container in the background docker_id=$(docker run -d --privileged=true my_rt_image /usr/bin/chrt -f 1 /path/to/my_app)
# 3. Extract the root Process ID (PID) of the running container container_pid=$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Pid}}' ${docker_id})
# 4. Migrate the container into the isolated cgroup # Moving the root PID automatically migrates its child threads in v2 echo ${container_pid} > /sys/fs/cgroup/rtcpus/cgroup.procs
# --- Workload is now running on isolated RT CPUs ---
# 5. Clean up when finished: Stop and remove the container docker stop ${docker_id} docker rm ${docker_id}
# 6. Tear down the shield and restore normal system scheduling ./shield.sh

note.title: Child processes are shielded by default
note.para: By writing the container's root Pid into the cgroup.procs file of the shielded cgroup, the unified hierarchy automatically tracks and confines all spawned child threads to your designated real-time CPUs.
